topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the lecture, sets expectations regarding nomenclature, and introduces the overall subject.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the complement system and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core principles, nomenclature rules, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms of the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways and how they converge on the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of the complement cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement eliminates pathogens, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the protective regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from destroying host cells.

topics.label: Clinical presentations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct medical pathologies and infection risks that arise when specific complement pathway components are deficient.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how bacterial pathogens evade complement clearance and how those evasion mechanisms are utilized in laboratory and clinical applications.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of the adaptive immune system
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
